sources.title: NHC HURDAT2 — Atlantic hurricane best tracks (storms that entered the Gulf, 2015→)
notes: Storm tracks are NHC best tracks (HURDAT2) through the 2025 season. Deferred volume and months to recover are estimates from monthly regulator data, relative to the mean of the 3 months before the storm, for hubs within 150 km of the track; recovery means back to 90% of that baseline. A dip can have other causes, such as a planned turnaround, so these are not reported shut-in volumes.

sources.title: NHC active storms — current Atlantic systems, forecast track and cone
notes: Live storm risk is a snapshot of the NHC active-storms feed taken when the pipeline last ran, not a real-time feed. Production in the path sums the latest reported month for hubs inside the forecast cone or near the forecast track; it is not a forecast of shut-ins. For decisions, use nhc.noaa.gov.

sources.title: Peer benchmark — production by operator of record, all operators (BOEM OGOR-A, NSTA PPRS, Sodir)
sources.license: US Government work; Open Government Licence v3.0; NLOD 2.0
notes: Peer benchmark: gross (100%) production by operator of record, not equity or net production. An operator is credited with the whole field or lease. Legal entities are grouped only by the table in pipeline/atlas/peers.py; BOEM and NSTA label history with each company's current name. Gulf deepwater means leases wholly in 1,000 ft (305 m) of water or more.

sources.title: BOEM / BSEE Data Center — boreholes and directional surveys (Shell-operated, deepwater)
sources.publisher: US Bureau of Ocean Energy Management
notes: Well paths are BOEM directional surveys (837 of 875 Shell-operated deepwater boreholes), simplified so that no surveyed point is more than about 5 m from the drawn path. Depths are below sea level (kelly bushing elevation subtracted). Boreholes without a survey are drawn as a straight schematic from the seabed to the reported bottom-hole location and are labelled as such. The seabed in the subsea view is interpolated from the water depths recorded at borehole sites, not a bathymetric survey.
